rounds.strongest_objection: Following each connected survivor for up to twelve cuts would start a further experiment after the registered four-cut endpoint. A finite null cannot settle all subsequent cuts.
rounds.response: Stop fresh six-knot growth at four cuts. Preserve every survivor, each initial or first split in its live groups, actual witness holdings and the scope of any all-age structural argument. Use the previously reported five-knot sixth-cut closure only as a control.

rounds.strongest_objection: Whole closure and a failure to close through four cuts have different implications. Several spanning trees can also lead to the same physical source.
rounds.response: Separate measured cuts from structural proofs, verify founder legality, count spanning-tree origins and test a reversed sign only on its reached zero-grant closure.

rounds.strongest_objection: A source label can have the same frequency in two comparisons while revealing different pointer states when its value is known. One pair of correlated keeper answers can also arise from a shared classical seed.
rounds.response: Test every subnormalised source block for the records actually delivered to the readers, including failures. Specify the physical cut, real workspace, coarse and repeated reads, and check shared classical, disclosed-label and passive one-site recoding controls.

rounds.strongest_objection: A continuing shared reference or a readable winding label can mimic a relation between two independent pointers.
rounds.response: Disconnect the source before local measurements, condition on each delivered outcome, trace both real instruments including repeated writes, and identify the separately prepared reference pair in the positive resource control.
